_doc: v3 settings for the lrmc (LANCE-19): rigid vehicle, moving parts split out by tools/art/v3/veh_prep.py from lrmc_prep.json (work dir lrmc_tracks), fit from tools/art/v3/lrmc_veh.json via v3_rigid.py.
name: lrmc

source.title: Heavy LRM Carrier
source.author: RGriffin65
source.notes: Vehicle rework (LANCE-19, 2026-10-30), differs from the mech text above: no joints or actuators. TRACKED kit: MC2's lrmc is a wheeled truck, but the approved v1 source is RGriffin65's tracked Heavy LRM Carrier and is kept. The fit is level (no ICP, `no_icp` in lrmc_veh.json; the v1 ICP pitched it 15 degrees). The kit's fused hull was split by `tools/art/v3/veh_prep.py` (lrmc_prep.json) into the hull, the turret ring (`lrmc_turret`, turns about the vertical axis), the LRM rack (`LrmPods`, the gun: elevates about its rear trunnion) and two track belts (`track_l`, `track_r`: the faces within 130 mm of the closed belt path round the wheels). The nine wheels a side (four road wheels, front and rear end wheels, three return rollers; `wheel_l0`..`wheel_r8`) are OWN GEOMETRY (`make_wheel`: tyre drum, recessed rim, hub boss, bolts) on axles fitted to the kit's wheel circles; the kit's wheel faces were cut from the hull. This own geometry is part of the CC BY-SA 4.0 derivative. The model's turret, rack and muzzle pivots were moved to the kit's turret ring and rack (node positions in the glb). Welded at 3 mm and planar-dissolved at 8 degrees, no collapse; belts on a tread strip of two link pitches (0.58 m) by `veh_lowpoly.py`.
